pr_body:
It looks like it is possible for a request to throw an exception early
before any API interaciton has happened. This can lead to the request count
map containing a `null` for the request count key.
The assertion is not correct and we should not NPE here
(as that might also hide the original exception since we are running this code in
a `finally` block from within the S3 SDK).

Closes #61670
pr_title: Cleanly Handle S3 SDK Exceptions in Request Counting
pr_comment:
Thanks @fcofdez !


> I'm not sure if we should take a deeper look into this to ensure that we're (or the SDK) not over/under accounting some requests?

I don't think this issue necessarily suggests a mistake in our counting unless this issue can be triggered without an exception on the SDK level. Since we do have tests that verify the exact request counts via the REST mock I think we're good in so far that  we're probably not missing any requests during regular operation. Also, as I mentioned this exception has never come up on Cloud as far as I can see, leading me to assume that it really just is some weird corner case where we throw early because of some broken configuration/bug?

That said in general, it would be nice to know the bug/environment that triggered this for sure currently I don't see a good strategy for reproducing this (the steps in the initial issue don't reproduce)?

@original-brownbear btw we have seen this in cloud now - see
https://github.com/elastic/sdh-cloud/issues/5711
and
https://us-east-1-logging-production-cloud.elastic.co/goto/16d18409fb4bd0e4fd2076ba3c337557

review_comment: This has never happened on Cloud ever and I believe the original issue reporting this is likely some error with the credentials or an S3 SDK bug (can't reproduce it) but I still think we should log it as we really only get here if there's a problem.
Yes, that seems strange. I took a quick glance to the SDK code and it seems like `AWSRequestMetrics` is created before the request is executed 🤔 as long as the collector is enabled for that request.

> seems like AWSRequestMetrics is created before the request is executed thinking 

The problem is that the counter is only there if an actual request was executed. Now if there is some bug (like we had before with an NPE in some URL utility method in the SDK) or legitmate exception (maybe from auth/signing) before that we never get the expected counter itself.
